_notes: Generated by /mrweirdo-onboard from resume + self-introduction + explicit hard-boundary answers.
Private user state only. Never commit a real user's essay_profile.json.
Use this as the source of truth for cover letters and essay questions; do not invent claims outside these facts.

avoid_claims: Do not claim domain experience, certifications, legal eligibility, GPA, awards, or employment relationships unless present in resume or explicit user answers.

why_role_bank._notes: Keys should be derived from this user's target functions, e.g. product, growth, operations, data, design, engineering, clinical, research.

why_industry_bank._notes: Keys should be derived from this user's real interests or resume trajectory.

hard_no_claims: clinical or regulated professional experience unless explicitly present
relatives or prior employment at a target company unless explicitly present

dynamic_questions_to_ask_later.trigger: many applications ask the same unfilled essay theme
dynamic_questions_to_ask_later.question: Ask one batch-level question, then reuse the answer across matching roles with job-specific tailoring.

_notes: Recurring NON-INFERABLE fields ATS forms require that must NEVER be invented — only filled from a confirmed user-provided value, otherwise the row is skipped with a precise gap reason.

onboard should surface any 'unknown' field to the user UPFRONT (batched) so the auto-apply loop does not stall mid-application. Each field: status one of 'unknown' | 'provided' | 'declined'; when 'provided', value holds the confirmed answer.
These complement (do not replace) profile.json. They are the facts that essays/cover-letters cannot ground and the scorer cannot guess.

permanent_address.note: Some forms (esp. onsite/co-op roles) require a permanent/residential street address distinct from school address. Ask-or-skip; never fabricate.

social_handles.note: Social-media / creator roles request public handles beyond LinkedIn. Only fill handles the user confirms are real and public; skip the row if a required handle is unknown.

compensation_acceptance.note: Distinct from the answer_bank 'compensation_expectations' soft text. Two ask-or-skip cases: (1) a posting states a specific figure and asks the candidate to accept/confirm it; (2) a required numeric field (input[type=number]) asks the candidate to STATE their salary/stipend expectation — the neutral sentence will be rejected by a number input. Both are personal decisions: ask the user for a figure or skip the row; never fabricate a number.

third_party_accounts.note: Some product/community roles require a real account/profile on their own platform (e.g. a game profile, a marketplace seller ID). Ask-or-skip; never invent an account identifier.

personal_preferences.note: Subjective questions tied to the user's real taste/opinion (favorite brands, what content they think is viral, hot takes). These are NOT inferable from a resume. Ask the user for one batch answer per theme, or skip; never fabricate an opinion that could surface in an interview.

cover_letter_path.note: Forms with a required separate cover-letter file input. If absent, the driver should not silently reuse the resume for a required cover-letter field without logging the decision.

onsite_location_logistics.note: SPECIFIC-CITY onsite LOGISTICS facts are ask-or-skip, distinct from general relocation WILLINGNESS (which is covered by search_intent.geographic_preference.relocation_policy / willing_to_relocate_for_internship). Questions like 'do you have reliable transportation to our <City> office?' or 'do you currently live/reside/are located in/near <City>?' assert a personal residence/transport fact the tool cannot know — never auto-answer them. Only auto-answer a named-city logistics question when that city (lowercased substring match) appears in confirmed_cities, which the user must explicitly confirm. A GENERAL 'are you willing to relocate?' or onsite-willingness question is NOT governed by this field — that is the relocation policy.
